# Rayner explainers

> Step-through explainers made with Rayner. Each page has a JSON file beside it, from `describeExplainer`: every case and step, with its title, caption, the state the scene recorded, what the step changed, and the resting picture in words and drawn as text.

Each item links the page, gives the first sentence of its first caption, and links its JSON.

## Explainers

- [Why does the periodic table have this shape?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/periodic-groups): Sodium is element 11, in group 1. JSON: [periodic-groups.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/periodic-groups.json)
- [Why does a deleted dictionary slot need a marker?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/python-dict): This dict uses an index and a separate entry table: a slot points to the entry holding its key and value. JSON: [python-dict.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/python-dict.json)
- [Why does a Bloom filter answer “maybe”?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/bloom-filter): A sign-up form checks each name a person types against the accounts database, one database read per check, and a read for a free name finds nothing. JSON: [bloom-filter.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/bloom-filter.json)
- [Why does a merge sometimes need a new commit?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/git-branches): Both branches started at A, where colour.txt is blue. JSON: [git-branches.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/git-branches.json)
- [Why can an older search replace the latest result?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/latest-search): Each keystroke starts a search, so “ca” starts first and “cat” second, and the user now wants “cat”. JSON: [latest-search.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/latest-search.json)
- [Why does the host’s rule change the odds of switching?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/monty-hall): A car is behind one of three doors, and goats are behind the other two. JSON: [monty-hall.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/monty-hall.json)
- [How many people make a shared birthday likely?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/birthday-paradox): A year has 365 days, so a match can seem to need a crowd. JSON: [birthday-paradox.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/birthday-paradox.json)
- [Why does one version of a tune sound off the beat?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/melody-rhythm): Each rectangle is a note: left to right is time, height is pitch and width is how long it sounds. JSON: [melody-rhythm.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/melody-rhythm.json)
- [Why does the north have summer when Earth is farthest from the Sun?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/seasons): Earth’s orbit is slightly oval, so it passes nearest the Sun once a year and farthest half a year later. JSON: [seasons.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/seasons.json)
- [Why does sunset line up with Manhattan’s streets?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/henge): Look west down a straight street. JSON: [henge.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/henge.json)
- [Why stealing an authorization code is not enough](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/oauth-pkce): A mobile or desktop app often gets its authorization code back as a redirect to a custom URI scheme. JSON: [oauth-pkce.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/oauth-pkce.json)
- [What does Git store when a file changes?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/exgit): hello.txt contains hello followed by a newline. JSON: [exgit.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/exgit.json)
- [How does a token bucket let a burst through but refuse a flood?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/token-bucket): A server shares its work among many clients, so it limits each one: a request it serves gets 200, OK, and one it refuses gets 429, Too Many Requests, which tells the client to slow down. JSON: [token-bucket.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/token-bucket.json)
- [What is a statechart, and why use one instead of a state machine?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/statecharts): This coffee machine is always in exactly one of four boxes: idle, grinding, brewing or ready. JSON: [statecharts.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/statecharts.json)
- [How does a ring buffer reuse storage?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ring-buffer): The simplest queue keeps its values in order in an array. JSON: [ring-buffer.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ring-buffer.json)
- [Can an agent use a key it never sees?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/2password): The app needs API_KEY in its environment. JSON: [2password.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/2password.json)
- [When should a short-lived certificate renew?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/cert-renewal): The CA/Browser Forum caps how long a public TLS certificate may last: 398 days until 15 March 2026, 200 from then, 100 from March 2027 and 47 from March 2029. JSON: [cert-renewal.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/cert-renewal.json)
- [Comment les parts changent-elles l’impôt d’un couple ?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/quotient-familial): Un couple marié ou pacsé, un enfant, déclare 65 673,88 € de revenu net imposable pour 2024. JSON: [quotient-familial.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/quotient-familial.json)
- [Can this Rust value cross a thread boundary?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/send-sync): x is an Arc, the pointer the standard library provides for sharing one value between threads; here it holds a Cell<i32>. thread::spawn runs a closure on a new thread, and move hands x to that closure. rustc refuses with error E0277, and the error names two traits: Sync, which Cell<i32> lacks, and Send, which Arc<Cell<i32>> needed for the move. JSON: [send-sync.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/send-sync.json)
- [Why does a GTFS route have no departures today?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/gtfs): Google publishes a sample GTFS feed, the CSV files a transit agency gives trip planners, for an invented Demo Transit Authority with 5 bus routes. JSON: [gtfs.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/gtfs.json)
- [Why can int4 and int8 rows take the same space?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/pg-page): Postgres stores a table in pages of 8192 bytes, and every page starts with a 24-byte header, so an empty page has 8168 bytes free. JSON: [pg-page.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/pg-page.json)
- [How does traffic policy divide requests among pods?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/traffic-policy): A Service of type LoadBalancer: a cloud load balancer sends outside requests to the nodes, and rules that kube-proxy writes on each node hand every request to a pod. JSON: [traffic-policy.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/traffic-policy.json)
- [Does isdigit guarantee int can parse it?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/isdigit): Python’s int() turns text into a whole number and raises ValueError when it cannot. JSON: [isdigit.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/isdigit.json)
- [What does a guest’s calendar keep when one meeting of a series changes?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ical-recurrence): Alice’s calendar app saves her stand-up as one VEVENT. JSON: [ical-recurrence.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ical-recurrence.json)
- [Where does an empty ext4 filesystem’s space go?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ext4-space): We ran mkfs.ext4 1.47.3 with no options on an empty 1 TiB disk, 268,435,456 blocks of 4096 bytes, mounted it and asked the kernel’s statfs, which df reads. JSON: [ext4-space.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ext4-space.json)
- [Which address should Express call the client?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/trust-proxy): Requests are meant to reach Express through a CDN and then a load balancer, so every connection Express sees comes from the load balancer, 10.0.0.5. req.ip is meant to be the sender’s address instead. JSON: [trust-proxy.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/trust-proxy.json)
- [Will this Tailwind colour fit the display?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/tailwind-gamut): Tailwind CSS 4 writes cyan-500 as oklch(71.5% 0.143 215.221): lightness, chroma and hue, where chroma is how far the colour stands from grey. JSON: [tailwind-gamut.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/tailwind-gamut.json)

## How these are made

- [How do I write that in Rayner?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/feature-tour): Each feature takes a few lines of the scene, and the picture they leave at rest is what a reader who opens the step from a link sees. JSON: [feature-tour.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/feature-tour.json)
- [How can a still skip the frames before it?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/lantern): A direct link opens a later picture without playing the earlier steps. JSON: [lantern.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/lantern.json)
- [Why build the page before readers open it?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/fork): The token-bucket page offers 1, 2, 4 tokens a second, the only rates its reader can choose. JSON: [fork.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/fork.json)
- [What does a Mermaid verifier check?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/agentic-mermaid): A cache hit follows yes to Database, while no leads straight to Reply. JSON: [agentic-mermaid.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/agentic-mermaid.json)
- [Why does the same text take different space?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/glyph): At size 0.9, “Hello, outlines” is 6.02 units wide in Inter and 8.10 in JetBrains Mono. JSON: [glyph.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/glyph.json)
- [Why must font measurement match the drawn face?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/font-metrics): Both rows draw “Ink on paper” in EB Garamond. JSON: [font-metrics.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/font-metrics.json)
- [Can hand-drawn strokes keep a diagram’s layout?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/pen-and-pencil): The words stayed where the layout placed them, but 5 of 8 poke out of their boxes. JSON: [pen-and-pencil.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/pen-and-pencil.json)
